rows.en: Yamato: "...Well, we're back for now, but..."
Touya: "Shall we head to the bridge?"
Yamato: "Yeah."
Kururu: "Ah! Found you!"
Kururu: "Hey, hey, Spirit Mechs really are amazing!"
Touya: "Yeah..."
Kururu: "So let me ride the Zeifon."
Touya: "Huh?"
Kururu: "Celica explains things to me,
but she won't let me get in."
Celica: "...Of course not.
Spirit Mechs aren't toys, you know?"
Kururu: "I don't think they are!
And I can pilot one properly!"
Celica: "No! If you broke it and another battle
started, we'd be in trouble. The only spare
we've got left is the Forstin..."
Kururu: "...Hmm."
Kururu: "What? There's a Spirit Mech with no pilot assigned?!"
Celica: "Oh..."
Kururu: "Hey, let me ride it! Let me!"
Celica: "No!"
Kururu: "Let me! Let me! Let me! Let me! Let me! Let me!"
Celica: "No means no!"
Kururu: "Stingy!"
Celica: "Call me stingy, but it's still no!"
Kururu: "...Sniff."
Celica: "Crying won't help."
Kururu: "What's your problem?! Oh! I get it!
You're not confident in it? Or is it defective? How awful!
Hiding your own failure and trying to blame someone else!"
Celica: "Wh-What did you say?!"
Kururu: "Huh? Am I wrong? Then it should be
fine for me to get in, right? Besides, are
Spirit Mechs so fragile they'd break from just that?"
Celica: "Grrrr... If you're going to go that far,
try it! If you manage to start it up, Touya
will teach you the basics! We're going to the hangar!"
Touya: "H-Hey!"
Kururu: "Yay! Come on, let's go!"
Touya: "H-Hey, don't pull my hand!
...Honestly, she fell for such a simple trick..."
Yamato: "You're hardly one to talk, Touya, meow..."
Touya: "Did you say something?"
Yamato: "No, nothing! Come on, let's go."
Kururu: "Hey, hey, it started!"
Celica: "..."
Touya: "It started up easily."
Yamato: "Yeah, it did."
Kururu: "Hey, you promised!
You're going to teach me to pilot it, right?"
Celica: "...I'll leave the rest to you."
Touya: "H-Hey, Celica!"
Kururu: "Come on, Touya! Hurry!"
Touya: "But..."
Thora: "...Touya."
Kururu: "Oh, Mom!"
Thora: "...Once she sets her mind on something, she won't listen...
I'm sorry, but would you help her?"
Touya: "Y-Yes. All right."
Kururu: "That's a pretty lecherous look in your eyes."
Touya: "...So this works like this..."
Kururu: "Huh? Then this goes like this?"
Touya: "Y-Yeah... And then..."
Kururu: "...I see... Then, like this!"
Yamato: "Amazing... Is this really your first Spirit Mech?"
Kururu: "Yep."
Yamato: "Maybe she's got more talent than Touya, meow?"
Touya: "Yeah. She's impressive."
Kururu: "Ahem!"
Touya: "..."
Yamato: "...She's already mastered all the basics.
And she's practicing on her own in simulated training mode...
Looks like she's having the time of her life, meow."
Thora: "Thank you, Touya."
Touya: "N-No problem... But why?"
Thora: "I don't really want her to learn to pilot
either. But she's also Grad Burgley's daughter.
A warrior's blood runs in her veins. I can't oppose
something she's decided for herself."
Touya: "But she's satisfied with simulated training for now.
Next, she'll probably demand to pilot it for real."
Thora: "Knowing her, she certainly might.
But parents aren't always right.
I believe a parent's role is to give their full support to what their child
has judged for themselves and believes is right.
To stand by them, even if the whole world
turns against them."
Touya: "So you're saying it can't be helped?"
Thora: "Of course I'm worried. Once she knows how to pilot it,
naturally she'll want to do it for real. In a crisis,
she might climb aboard and fight without hesitating."
Touya: "Then..."
Thora: "...If I could, I'd keep her by my side even if I had to
lock her up. But that's a parent's selfishness. It would only be forcing
my own wishes on her and pretending it's for her sake..."
Touya: "You really love her, don't you?"
Thora: "There's no parent who doesn't love their child.
Touya, please look after Kururu."
Touya: "Yes. If you're happy with me.
I'll help until we reach Flamuelk Castle, at least."
